description: Staircase sphere, Re=U*D/nu=100, D3Q19 BGK + freeze-solid + half-way bounce-back + far_field_bc_3d. Drag taken from the Ladd (1994) momentum-exchange force 2*Sum_surface c_ix f_i restricted to the SURFACE solid cells (the cylinder_3d acceptance caliber). VERDICT: the surface-only caliber removes the historical all-solid blow-up but the sphere staircase still converges to Cd ~ +9%, far outside the 3% acceptance bar.
force_method: ladd_momentum_exchange (post-stream, pre-bounce-back); primary = surface cells only (solid with >=1 fluid 6-neighbour). Three calibers reported on the same field.
geometry: staircase parametric sphere, mask (i-cx)^2+(j-cy)^2+(k-cz)^2 <= R^2, R = D/2 cells

domain_blockage_probe.description: lateral 16 (blockage 6.25%) vs lateral 32 (blockage 3.125%) at D=10, identical run otherwise
domain_blockage_probe.verdict: bit-identical to 4 decimals => the lateral-domain / blockage lever is DEAD for the sphere surface-MEM; the residual error is not a blockage artifact.

cross_check_other_instruments.cv_momentum_balance: independent control-volume momentum-balance probes on the same staircase sphere read Cd_cov = 1.1985 (D=16) / 1.2130 (D=20), i.e. +9.8% / +11.1% vs SN - the SAME +9~11% as surface-MEM. Two independent instruments agree, so the residual is a geometry/resolution limit, not a MEM-caliber bug.
cross_check_other_instruments.pressure_plus_friction: -16.5% (D=16) / -25.9% (D=20): a different, systematically LOW caliber (staircase pressure integration misses the stagnation rise).
cross_check_other_instruments.historical_all_solid_mem: +264% at D=40 (GeneralSimEngine/MRT path) - a different implementation whose all-solid sum is interior-dominated; the present BGK Ladd chain has only a small interior term (0.02-0.06), so surface-only trims all-solid from +12.7% to +9.15% only.

cylinder_3d_contrast.cylinder_3d_verified: Cd +2.45% / -0.19% (D=20/40), surface-only Ladd MEM, span 2.64% - PASSES.
cylinder_3d_contrast.difference: (1) The cylinder is curved only in the xy cross-section and flat/invariant in z; the sphere is doubly curved, so the staircase mis-represents the surface in every direction and the interface MEM flux carries a larger consistent bias. (2) The sphere has a much larger interior/solid ratio (interior/total = 0.62 at D=12, 0.71 at D=18 vs the cylinder's thin wall ring), so the sphere is dominated by surface cells whose staircase normals are wrong. (3) measured consequence: on the cylinder the surface-only caliber moves the answer INTO the reference cluster; on the sphere it removes the interior pseudo-term but the surface value itself is already +9% high.

why_it_fails: The staircase sphere with the volumetric mask over-estimates the interface momentum flux; the surface-only MEM (and, independently, the control-volume instrument) both converge to Cd ~ 1.19 (+9%) and stay there for all feasible D (12..18). The error is a converged GEOMETRY bias, not a mesh-resolution deficit and not a blockage artifact. Reaching the 3% bar needs a smooth-boundary representation (the historical octree R10 hit +1.59% but at 0.03 steps/s, infeasible) or D >~ 30 with the 3D memory ceiling (~15 GiB/device => D<=~18 at lateral 32).

grid_B_D18.note: in flight at write time, tracking D=12

two_grids.note: mesh-converged to the WRONG value: span < 3% but both grids ~+9%.

acceptance: every checkpoint within 3% AND mesh-converged (two grids, span <=3%). sphere_re100 satisfies convergence (span 0.23%) but NOT accuracy (~+9%).
